items.title: Wendy Oxenhorn interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 22, 2026
items.q: It makes me think of John Levy, who managed Joe Williams and Nancy Wilson and Cannonball Adderley.

ctx.x: the love of my life. You know? So you have to understand the sequence. So here I was without the blues and then look what happened because of that experience, because of taking care of the old man, building a business, getting him to be financially independent from the blues. I was able to have what I needed to relate, and also having been a musician for the year. You know I worked in the train stations where when it was sweltering, you know, the old man used to keep a bag of ice under his little bowler hat. You…

It makes me think of John Levy, who managed Joe Williams and Nancy Wilson and Cannonball Adderley. And he had been a musician, he had been a bassist with a number of people and I know Joe used to say, “Well that made him a good manager for me because he knew the routine. He knew the challenges and how to deal with musicians, etcetera.”
